literal.prompt: Лист какого дерева изображён в центре национального флага Канады?

literalGroups.primaryGround: Canada.ca L41 and L54-L58 explicitly identify the central flag emblem as a maple leaf. The four answer labels are all tree names: Canada.ca supports maple; Arnold Arboretum L40-L47 supports oak/acorn; NPS L38-L40 identifies paper birch; Morton L139 and L175-L184 identifies quaking aspen and its leaves. The stem asks for a broad, recognizable tree identity, not a park location.
literalGroups.locator: Canada.ca L41, L54-L58; Arnold Arboretum L40-L47; NPS L38-L40; Morton Arboretum L139, L175-L184

literalGroups.literal: Это клён: правительство Канады описывает центральный знак флага как стилизованный красный кленовый лист. Этот лист используют как символ канадской идентичности с XIX века.
literalGroups.primaryGround: Canada.ca L41 names the central stylized red maple leaf, and L56 states the maple leaf has represented Canadian identity since the 19th century. Both claims directly support the two sentences.

literalGroups.literal: Стилизованный лист имеет 11 концов; вариант с 13 концами заменили, чтобы символ легче узнавался издали.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The source says the current stylized maple leaf has 11 points; the original 13-point design was changed because it was hard to recognize at a distance or in wind.

literalGroups.literal: Плоды дубов называют желудями; у разных видов они созревают за один или два сезона.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The page describes acorns as oak fruit and states oaks may take one or two growing seasons to mature an acorn.

literalGroups.literal: У бумажной берёзы тонкая белая кора отслаивается полосами и отражает зимнее солнце.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS states paper birch bark is thin, peeling, curly and white, reflecting most sunlight and heat away from the tree.

literalGroups.literal: Плоские черешки заставляют листья осины дрожать на ветру и шелестеть.
literalGroups.primaryGround: Morton Arboretum says flattened petioles let quaking-aspen leaves tremble in wind and create rustling sound.

correctNoteNewFact.fact: The flag leaf has eleven points; the first thirteen-point version was changed because it was harder to recognize at a distance and in wind. This is a concrete design fact beyond the prompt and answer.

entries.absoluteDifficulty: easy: recognizing the maple leaf as the central symbol on the Canadian national flag is broad adult cultural knowledge rather than park-tourism familiarity or specialist botany. All four choices are familiar trees of the same category; the task asks for a single familiar national emblem, without multistep inference.
